title.narrative: Enhanced institutional capacities of constituents to design and implement integrated employment policies for the creation of decent jobs for youth and women, including IDPs.

description.narrative: Following the adoption of the Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP) for South Sudan 2023-2025 by the tripartite constituents on October 16th, 2023, the Minister of Labour (MoL) called the ILO to support them in the formulation and implementation of a National Employment Policy (NEP). The policy should highlight key programmatic areas and help direct resources in a cooperative manner across government departments as well as securing international support and technical assistance in its implementation. The strategy involves establishing a national tripartite inter-ministerial committee and a technical committee that brings together the pertinent line ministries, workers and employers’ organizations as well as some international partners and UN agencies to provide inputs and inform the formulation of the NEP for South Sudan. Broad based consultations involving all actors concerned (including the States) will take place to inform about the key issues to tackle to promote full and productive employment. The CPO also intends to address the lack of reliable data and statistics in South Sudan on the level of employment/unemployment and the impacts of internal/external conflicts and natural disasters on economic activities and employment, not least to contribute an evidence base to the NEP discussions. The methodology proposed is to rely on remote sensing data, to overcome the lack of reliable census data and household data. The ILO works closely with the UN Agencies in South Sudan to ensure complementarity and collaboration and produce an impact assessment of conflicts on economic activities and the labour market in South-Sudan over the period 2012-2023, which then informs the NEP formulation process.
